# architecture-components

Gives every product source one owner among the components the components view draws. It keeps the references between components, and the runtimes that reach them, to what the view draws. It reads the model `architecture-contract` describes and adds no fields or columns.

## Owners

A component owns the product sources its claims cover: a path in its diagram strings or its callout row. Boundaries, people, and external systems own nothing; their claims only scope the components inside them.

Product sources are the product category of the `architecture-contract` inventory, so tests, tools, and generated files need no owner. These sources are tools:

- A root-level file a language module names a tool config; the same file deeper down is product code.
- A source under the top-level `scripts/` folder.
- A file only a manifest's scripts run, as the language module that reads the manifest finds it.
- Neither of the last two when the product starts it or publishes it.

Ownership fails or holds as follows:

- A product source no component names fails, naming the source.
- Agent tooling folders, such as `.claude/` and `.codex/`, get no exemption: their sources need an owner, and their references a drawn edge.
- A code span or label claims a root-level source by its bare name; any other bare name stays prose.
- A source two components name, in two diagrams of one view, fails naming both claims. Two claims in one diagram fail in `architecture-contract`.
- A claimed path that no longer exists fails in `architecture-contract`.

## References

Every reference between two owners is an observed edge. The view must draw it, from the component or a boundary enclosing it to the other component or a boundary enclosing that one. An edge the view does not draw fails at the reference, naming the view and any drawn edge in the other direction. A drawn edge no reference uses is allowed.

Each [language module](../../internal/lang/langs/langs.go) whose view reader lists references finds them in its product sources. A reference is an import of another folder, or a name that resolves to a declaration in another file. The reader's package, `go/internal/lang/<language>/views`, documents how it resolves them.

Comments and string literals create no reference. A source its reader cannot parse fails. A reference under a build condition keeps it, and the error names it after `under`. Generated sources stay in the inventory but are not read.

## Evidence

An edge row that links a source file requires the edge; a row without a link allows it. The link must be a source whose reader lists references, owned by the edge's first component. Its lines, or the whole file without an anchor, must name the second component: import its folder, or name a symbol it declares. Anything else fails, naming the row and the link.

For an external system the lines must name it outside comments, by a word of its name, technology, or description.

## Runtimes

The runtimes are the products `architecture-containers` matches to containers. A component under a boundary whose ID is a container of the containers view belongs to that runtime. Each runtime is walked from the components its product folders are built from, along the observed edges.

Reaching a component declared under another runtime's container fails at the reference, naming that boundary. A component outside every container boundary is shared and may be reached by any runtime.

## Scope

A test, changelog or doc change cannot move the views. So a scoped run with no changed view, requirement doc, product or tool source, manifest or `.gitattributes` passes with zero files. Every other run reads the whole model and every product source, so a change to one side still meets the other.

## Requirements

[Requirement 0075](../../../docs/requirements/0075-checks-architecture-components.md) has one installed-command test per acceptance.
